claims.text_en: Khet Bang Phlat (บางพลัด, geocode 1070) is a west-bank (Thonburi) khet of 11.360 km2 with four khwaeng: Bang Phlat 3.296 km2 (21,450 residents), Bang O 2.846 km2 (23,691), Bang Bamru 2.332 km2 (17,373), Bang Yi Khan 2.886 km2 (24,691); registered population 87,205 at Dec 2023 per Thai Wikipedia's DOPA-based table (the app's 89,417 is a different vintage). The name's folk origin is from displaced people 'พลัดหลง' (losing their way) after the 1767 fall of Ayutthaya. It was split from khet Bangkok Noi on 9 Nov 1989 (พ.ศ. 2532); areas of Bang Bamru/Bang Yi Khan south of Borommaratchachonnani Road were returned to Bangkok Noi on 12 Dec 1991; a 2002 idea to rename the khet 'บางภัทร์' was never adopted. OSM relations corroborate: khet relation 2942281 and exactly four khwaeng relations 11355125-28.

claims.text_en: Four MRT Blue Line stations sit inside khet Bang Phlat: Bang Yi Khan (BL05), Sirindhorn (BL06), Bang Phlat (BL07) and Bang O (BL08). Thai Wikipedia lists all four as being in the khet (with an editorial note that it matched them to like-named khwaeng), and an OSM area query independently found the station nodes 3801037853 (บางยี่ขัน), 6563228219 (สิรินธร), 3801037852 (บางพลัด) and 3801037855 (บางอ้อ) inside khet area 3602942281. Charan 13 station (BL02) lies further south along Charan Sanitwong Road and was NOT returned inside any of the four khet areas in OSM data read - it likely falls on the Bangkok Yai/Bangkok Noi side of the boundary; whether it serves the khet edge is a polygon question the app decides. The SRT Light Red Line adds Bang Bamru station in khwaeng Bang Bamru (Thai Wikipedia).

claims.text_en: Counter-evidence to an unqualified transport story: Bang Phlat MRT station (BL07) was the least-used station on the entire MRT Blue Line in 2021, with 485,490 passengers for the year (English Wikipedia, citing 2021 data). The Blue Line extension opened through the khet only on 4 December 2019, so the ridership base is young; transport 8 is supported by station count inside the khet, but station usage data read points to demand concentrated elsewhere (e.g., Bang O/Sirindhorn toward the Pin Klao side) - per-station split within the khet is unverified.

The score of 6 is honest-low: one quality riverside park, very small share of land, remainder of green mostly temple grounds and roadside trees (unsourced).

claims.text_en: Nightlife-8 test (the stated tension): app counts 56 nightlife venues vs 763 food venues in an 89k-resident khet that both travel guides describe as non-touristic and quiet ('The neighborhood is non-touristic area for international tourists' - Explorenique). 56 venues is a mid-sized count, not a nightlife district; the plausible suppliers are the Charan Sanitwong / Pin Klao commercial strip - Thai Wikipedia names Pata Pin Klao, Major Cineplex Pinklao, Lotus Charan Sanitwong and Tang Hua Seng as the khet's business anchors (several sit at the khet edge; app polygons decide). Researcher inference: nightlife 8 reads high for the district's family character and likely reflects corridor-adjacent venues rather than an internal scene; count-versus-score consistency cannot be fully tested without per-venue placement.

claims.text_en: Landmark frame: Rama VIII Bridge opened 7 May 2002 - 475 m long, single 160 m tower, Thailand's first asymmetric cable-stayed bridge - linking Phra Nakhon (Wisut Kasat Rd) with Bang Phlat district, with a park at its Thonburi foot (Renown Travel). Thai Wikipedia adds that Rama VI, Rama VII and Krung Thon bridges also touch the khet, and lists hospitals (Yanhee; the Ear-Eye-Nose-Throat hospital) and 23 temples (incl. Wat Wimutidham, Wat Paorohit, Wat Awuth Wiksitararam), plus the Rama VI-era Bang-or Mosque built by Persian merchant descendants on Charan Sanitwong soi 86 (Explorenique).

claims.text_en: Character (vibe 7, crowd 4): the khet is framed by guides as a non-touristic lower-inner-Thonburi area of 'hidden history' - temple communities along Charan Sanitwong sois (Wat Karuha Bodee soi 42, Wat Bowon Mongkhon soi 79), a khon-mask handicraft household workshop, the Galyani Vadhana music institution, and mosque-side gingerbread wooden houses - with the Rama VIII riverside park as its public face. Density figures (app 7,871/km2, TH wiki 7,676/km2 Dec 2023) are the second-lowest of the four khets in this batch, consistent with a low-crowd reading.

question_answers.notes: Khet Bang Phlat, 11.360 km2, 4 khwaeng (Bang Phlat 3.296 / Bang O 2.846 / Bang Bamru 2.332 / Bang Yi Khan 2.886 km2), split from Bangkok Noi 9 Nov 1989, 1991 boundary trim, OSM 2942281 + 4 khwaeng relations. Landmarks in: Suan Luang Rama VIII, Rama VIII bridge foot, 4 MRT Blue stations, Yanhee hospital, 23 temples, Bang-or Mosque. Charan 13 MRT station reads as outside the khet in OSM (app polygons decide).

Subarea daily lives distinguishable only at anchor level: station khwaengs (Bang Phlat/Bang O) = Charan retail spine; Bang Yi Khan = riverside park face; Bang Bamru = Light Red stop. Deeper per-khwaeng texture (markets, schools, street life) not found in bodies read.

Transport 8 supported by 4 in-khet Blue stations + Light Red Bang Bamru stop; counter-evidence: BL07 was the Blue Line's least-used station in 2021 (485,490 pax) - the extension's demand is young and uneven.

Main counter-view: nightlife 8 in a guide-described non-touristic, quiet family khet (56 venues, likely corridor-adjacent around Pin Klao/Charan); plus least-used-station evidence tempering the transport story.
No sourced annual/weekly festival calendar found. Cadence inferred: weekday Charan commute + weekend riverside park use; ceremonial temple calendar at 23 temples unsourced.

No walkability prose found in any body read. Station adjacency and Charan-street retail density imply short station-to-shop distances, but no radius-to-time conversions were made and none should be; sidewalks/footpath quality unsourced.

Daily-life anchors: Lotus Charan, Tang Hua Seng, Pata/Major at the Pin Klao edge (TH wiki business list); 622 marketed condo rentals; riverside park. Market-level detail (wet markets, fresh markets) absent from bodies read.

Rent 9 / 11,500-24,000: HipFlat Oct 2026 shows 622 listings, 1BR avg ~USD444 (~15.5k), 2BR ~USD701 (~24.5k). Editorial floor below portal 1BR average - plausible for older/unlisted stock; blend otherwise consistent.
Green 6 honest-low confirmed: 4.2 ha (0.4%) app figure; single identified public park (Suan Luang Rama VIII) inside khet per TH wiki + OSM; quiet reading supported by second-lowest density in batch.
Fits: quiet-west-bank seekers, families wanting cheaper rent with Blue Line access, riverside-park users. Poor fit: nightlife-first movers (scene thin and corridor-bound), car-free luxury seekers.
2024-2026 changes: none found in queries run for this khet specifically; big structural change (Blue extension) dates to Dec 2019; Light Red Bang Bamru stop ~2021. Absence limited to search coverage.

Outside-the-score: (a) khwaeng-level placement of Bang Phlat/Charan 13 stations unresolved in OSM read; (b) no local-news coverage read; (c) app venue counts not reproducible externally; (d) Walkability/rhythm gaps recorded rather than filled.

preview.text_en: A quiet west-bank khet with four MRT Blue stations, 23 temples and one riverside park - cheap by inner-Bangkok standards, and honest about it: its busiest new station was the Blue Line's least-used in 2021.

guide_lead.text_en: Bang Phlat is the low-key Thonburi side of the river that the MRT Blue Line reached only in December 2019. Its four stations - Bang Yi Khan, Sirindhorn, Bang Phlat, Bang O - put the khet on the rail map without turning it central: the 2021 counters still show Bang Phlat station as the Blue Line's quietest. Life here organizes around Charan Sanitwong Road's local retail spine, 23 temples, the Bang-or Mosque, and Suan Luang Rama VIII, one of the few public parks on the river's west bank. Rents sit well below central districts, and the trade-off is the same on every page read: little nightlife or tourist infrastructure, and parkland measured in single hectares.

strengths.text_en: Four MRT Blue stations inside the khet (Bang Yi Khan, Sirindhorn, Bang Phlat, Bang O) plus an SRT Light Red stop at Bang Bamru - rare west-bank rail coverage, corroborated by OSM node membership.
Affordable, real-stock rental market: 622 portal-listed condos averaging roughly 15.5k (1BR) and 24.5k (2BR) THB in Oct 2026, with cheaper unlisted stock beneath.

tradeoffs.text_en: The district's own headline station (BL07) was the Blue Line's least-used in 2021 - connectivity has not yet produced central-style demand, so service frequency and crowd energy should not be assumed.
Public green is a single riverside park on a 0.4% park share; the nightlife-8 reading rests on corridor venues rather than an internal scene.

conditional_fit.text_en: Choose Bang Phlat if you want Blue Line access and sub-25k 2BR rents on the quiet side of the river; the park and temple fabric reward walkers on weekends.
Avoid if a dense nightlife scene or walkable late-evening street life is the priority - the 8-rated nightlife count is corridor-dependent and the residential khwaengs read quiet in every source read.
